concrete_capability_transition: Brownie CLI moves from clean installed arbitrary-repository execution to restart-safe and recovery-safe installed execution: brownie resume can continue the intended persisted runtime-owned objective scope after interruption, response loss, or transport timeout without duplicate admission, unrelated task selection, or CLI-owned replay/recovery policy.

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Proves the installed CLI can recover long-running objective execution across restart and lost response by delegating scoped continuation to Rust runtime-owned persisted journey, progress, and recovery provenance.
Keeps resume and recovery execution on the existing runtime-owned task.run/headless.continue_once state machine rather than adding a CLI agent loop or CLI task-selection policy.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development by making installed brownie run workflows restart-safe and recovery-safe, while preserving Rust runtime authority over replay, continuation, and recovery provenance.
answers.new_capability: A caller can interrupt or lose the response from brownie run, start a later CLI process, and use brownie resume to continue the intended persisted runtime-owned objective scope without duplicate admission or unrelated task selection.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: CLI-7 stabilized output, CLI-8 added install/help, and CLI-9 proved clean arbitrary-repository completion. They do not prove restart/lost-response recovery, same-objective independent invocations, terminal-latest no-fallback behavior, or typed recovery/retry scoped resume.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: CLI product completion would lack evidence that long-running autonomous objectives can survive process loss or transport timeout without duplicate side effects or broad global resume selection.
answers.non_duplicative: CLI-10 is not output, install, or clean-run coverage. It validates restart/resume and recovery/retry scope semantics across process boundaries after CLI-7 through CLI-9.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The implementation uses existing task.list, headless.continue_once, headless.run.drive, and existing runtime-owned recovery/progress evidence. No new runtime RPC or passthrough is introduced.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. No report, readiness, digest, verdict, history, inspection, or summary surface is added.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Runtime scope derivation now treats typed recovery/retry provenance as part of the originating journey scope only when source and recovery handles match runtime-owned evidence, and fails closed on conflicts. CLI behavior remains thin and uses existing resume requests.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: External schedulers can safely resume CLI-driven objective execution after process loss or timeout, and runtime-created recovery/retry tasks stay in objective scope without CLI heuristics.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes CLI-10, the final open required CLI Product DoD gap before product completion evaluation, subject to passing PR review and zero blocking or required-before-release debt.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: CLI-10 updates the deterministic current phase manifest and runtime scoped resume behavior. Review must confirm typed recovery scope remains Rust-runtime-owned, fail-closed, and backed by behavior tests rather than wrapper-only evidence.

exit_criteria: After interrupted or response-lost brownie run, a later brownie resume continues the intended persisted runtime-owned CLI objective scope.
Same objective text can be run as multiple independent invocations without identity collision.
The same explicit persisted runtime invocation remains replay-safe without duplicate admission or side effects.
Terminal latest CLI objective does not cause resume to fall back to unrelated global eligible tasks.
Unrelated frontend/runtime tasks do not enter CLI resume scope.
Runtime-created recovery/retry tasks with typed provenance remain inside the original CLI objective scope even when parent_task_id and parent_run_id are absent.
Malformed, stale, conflicting, or ambiguous recovery provenance fails closed and never broadens by goal text, mode id, timestamp proximity, id similarity, objective text, or same workspace alone.
Real actual brownie and brownie-runtime binaries pass restart/resume and recovery/retry E2E tests from temporary ordinary repositories outside the Brownie source tree.
Objective transport timeout or CLI process loss is treated as transport/liveness only, not objective/task/product failure.
No new runtime RPC, generic passthrough, report, readiness, history, digest, verdict, summary, CLI-owned policy engine, or workspace mutation authority is introduced.
behavior_evidence: brownie-runtime scoped continuation tests prove latest CLI journey selection and terminal-latest no-fallback behavior remain runtime-owned.
brownie-runtime typed recovery scope tests prove parentless verification recovery and retry tasks are admitted to the originating CLI journey scope only through matching source/recovery provenance.
brownie-runtime negative tests prove conflicting recovery provenance remains no-eligible instead of broadening scoped resume.
brownie-cli installed real-binary restart/resume test proves a persisted CLI journey can survive lost response and later resume through the sibling runtime from an ordinary repository.
brownie-cli installed real-binary recovery test proves a runtime-created verification recovery task stays inside the original CLI objective scope and is selected by brownie resume.

accepted_capability: The Brownie CLI will resume interrupted or lost-response installed run workflows through runtime-owned persisted scope evidence.
Typed runtime-created recovery/retry tasks stay in the original CLI objective scope without CLI-owned recovery heuristics.
behavior_evidence: Focused runtime scoped continuation tests pass for typed recovery, typed retry, terminal latest no-fallback, and conflict fail-closed behavior.
Focused installed CLI binary/runtime tests pass for persisted restart-resume and runtime-created verification recovery scoped resume from ordinary repositories.
safety_boundary: No Core Runtime terminal campaign state is reopened or mutated.
No new runtime JSON-RPC method is added.
The CLI does not read ledgers, discover Mode Packs from files, evaluate permissions, select tasks, apply patches, or own recovery/replay policy.
Scoped recovery expansion is derived only from matching runtime-owned typed provenance and fails closed on conflicts.
non_goals: No new primary command, develop alias, generic RPC passthrough, report, readiness, history, digest, verdict, or inspection surface.
No Mode Pack, Product DoD, provider, permission, workspace mutation, replay, or fail-closed semantic redesign beyond bounded scope derivation.
No package publication, signing, notarization, Homebrew formula, or npm publication.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected CLI-owned recovery ancestry or task sorting because scoped resume must be runtime-owned.
Rejected goal-text, timestamp proximity, id similarity, and same-workspace matching because those would broaden scope heuristically.
Rejected fake-runtime-only acceptance because CLI-10 requires actual restart/resume and recovery/retry process evidence.
Rejected adding a new RPC because existing task.list and headless.continue_once already carry the continuation contract.
technical_debt: No new blocking or required_before_release debt is accepted by this phase.
CLI product completion remains blocked until CLI-10 is merged, full validation passes, and required gaps/debts are zero.
next_capability_rationale: After CLI-10 lands, evaluate CLI product completion instead of inventing additional CLI phases unless concrete blocking debt is discovered.
